title: International Defense Tender Arbitration, ICC Jurisdiction & Force Majeure
workplace_track: International Defense Tender Arbitration & ICC Contracts
description: Executive sales and contract legal engineering: drafting liquidated damages indemnities, managing ICC Paris arbitration clauses, navigating split liability under Incoterms 2020 DPU/DAP, and diplomatic de-escalation of foreign ministry disputes.
learning_objectives: Master mandative and formulaic subjunctive in international military procurement contracts
Formulate precise risk transfer stipulations under Incoterms 2020 rules
Utilize high-register diplomatic hedging in multi-million dollar defense contract negotiations

questions.prompt: Be it resolved that Tatra Trucks _____ harmless the defense ministry against any third-party patent infringement claims arising from the proprietary pneumatic suspension system.

explanations.correct: Formulaic legal subjunctive ('Be it resolved that [entity] hold harmless...') uses the bare base form 'hold' without third-person '-s' or modal auxiliary.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Shall hold' is standard contractual obligation, but follows standard clauses, not the archaic formulaic subjunctive preamble 'Be it resolved that'.
explanations.wrong_C: Indicative 'holds' violates the formulaic legal subjunctive mood.
explanations.wrong_D: Continuous aspect is completely inappropriate in legal indemnity deeds.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Budiž ujednáno, že Tatra Trucks odškodní...'. Formal legal preambles use formulaic subjunctive base forms: 'Be it resolved that Tatra Trucks hold harmless...'.

questions.prompt: Under the agreed Incoterms 2020 DPU (Delivered at Place Unloaded) terms, at what exact juncture _____ to the procurement authority?

options.text: the risk of accidental loss is transferring
does the risk of loss pass

explanations.correct: Formal interrogative syntax requires auxiliary inversion ('does the risk of loss pass') for clean, unambiguous commercial arbitration clarity.
explanations.wrong_A: Lacks required auxiliary verb 'does' in direct technical inquiry.
explanations.wrong_B: Indirect word order without inversion cannot form a direct question.
explanations.wrong_D: Inversion of full lexical verb ('passes the risk') is archaic and grammatically incorrect in modern commercial English.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'v jakém okamžiku přechází riziko škody na...?'. In English, questions require auxiliary 'does': 'At what exact juncture does the risk of loss pass...?'

questions.prompt: _____ the ministry to invoke the force majeure clause prematurely due to port customs congestion, our legal counsel would immediately initiate ICC expedited arbitration proceedings.

explanations.correct: Inverted second conditional ('Were the ministry to invoke...') denotes a formal hypothetical future contingency with dignified diplomatic distance.
explanations.wrong_B: 'If' would require standard word order ('If the ministry were to invoke...').
explanations.wrong_C: 'Had' pairs with past counterfactual participles, not the infinitive 'to invoke'.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Should' would be followed by bare infinitive 'invoke', not 'to invoke'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Kdyby ministerstvo předčasně uplatnilo...'. Formal diplomatic legal phrasing inverts 'were': 'Were the ministry to invoke...'.

questions.prompt: It is stipulated in section 14.2 that the supplier _____ penalty payments in the event that spare parts deliveries fail to achieve the 98% operational availability metric.

explanations.correct: Mandative subjunctive after passive verb of requirement ('It is stipulated that [entity] remit...') requires base verb 'remit'.
explanations.wrong_B: Third person singular 'remits' is indicative, whereas legal stipulations require the subjunctive base form.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Shall remit' is common in drafting, but when introduced by 'It is stipulated that...', the subjunctive bare form 'remit' is the most refined legal register.
explanations.wrong_D: Infinitive 'to remit' cannot stand as the main predicate of a 'that'-clause.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Je stanoveno, že dodavatel uhradí...'. English mandative subjunctive uses base form: 'It is stipulated that the supplier remit...'.

questions.prompt: Only by providing an unconditional standby letter of credit from an internationally rated tier-1 bank _____ the tender evaluation committee permit the bid bond exemption.

explanations.correct: Fronted restrictive phrase 'Only by providing...' requires subject-auxiliary inversion with future modal 'will' ('will the committee permit').
explanations.wrong_B: 'Does' refers to general habit, whereas tender evaluations are specific future conditional determinations.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Did' refers to completed past action, conflicting with the prospective tender evaluation process.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Would' requires a counterfactual condition, which is absent here.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Pouze předložením neodvolatelného akreditivu výbor povolí...'. In English, fronted 'Only by...' demands inversion: 'Only by providing... will the committee permit...'.

questions.prompt: Our negotiation posture must remain uncompromising regarding warranty ceilings, _____ we risk setting an adverse contractual precedent across all Eastern European defense tenders.

explanations.correct: Formal conjunction 'lest' ('for fear that / in order to avoid') introduces an adverse risk and pairs with subjunctive or indicative in elevated diplomatic English.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Otherwise' is an adverb requiring a semicolon or coordinator, not a subordinating conjunction.
explanations.wrong_C: 'In case' indicates precaution, not avoidance of a direct hazard.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Unless' means 'except if', which reverses the intended causal meaning.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'abychom neriskovali... / jinak hrozí, že...'. High-level diplomatic English uses 'lest' ('lest we risk setting an adverse precedent').

questions.prompt: No sooner had the bilateral tender contract been signed in Abu Dhabi _____ the ministry issued an addendum demanding supplementary cold-weather cabin modifications.

explanations.correct: 'No sooner had [action]... than [second action]' is the strictly required correlative pair in high-level English.
explanations.wrong_B: 'That' cannot introduce the temporal correlative clause.
explanations.wrong_C: 'As' is colloquial and grammatically invalid here.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Sotva byla smlouva podepsána, než ministerstvo vydalo dodatek'. Always pair 'No sooner had...' with 'THAN'.

questions.prompt: _____ the military attache inquire regarding our export licensing status under EU dual-use regulations, reassure him that our authorization dossier is already before the licensing board.

explanations.correct: Inverted first conditional ('Should the attache inquire...') represents formal diplomatic courtesy for possible future inquiries.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Were the attache to inquire' would be acceptable, but 'Were' cannot pair directly with bare infinitive 'inquire'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Could' cannot form an inverted conditional clause of this type.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Kdyby se vojenský atašé dotazoval...'. Formal diplomatic correspondence uses 'Should [subject] [base verb]...': 'Should the attache inquire...'.

questions.prompt: The arbitration panel ruled that the delayed vehicle commissioning was _____ attributable to port blockades rather than any defect in Tatra's powertrain components.

explanations.correct: In high-stakes dispute resolution, nuanced legal qualification ('principally attributable' = chiefly/primarily) accurately allocates proportional liability without absolute overclaiming.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Unquestionably' is rhetorically aggressive and weakens evidentiary arbitration credibility.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Unequivocally' is excessively absolute when dealing with multi-factor logistics delays.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Hardly' reverses the intended meaning, suggesting Tatra was to blame.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'převážně / v hlavní míře přičitatelné'. In arbitration findings, 'principally attributable' balances evidentiary accuracy and legal liability.

questions.prompt: Not for one moment _____ our commercial negotiation team consider conceding sovereign immunity jurisdiction to a local foreign domestic court.

explanations.correct: Fronted negative phrase 'Not for one moment' with past action verb 'consider' demands past auxiliary inversion 'did' ('Not for one moment did our team consider...').
explanations.wrong_A: 'Is' cannot pair with past lexical verb 'consider'.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Would' suggests hypothetical willingness rather than an emphatic historical fact.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Ani na jediný okamžik náš tým neuvažoval...'. Inverted negative construction: 'Not for one moment did our team consider...'.
